B14_00: Activation of the complement proteolytic cascade is restrained by soluble and membrane-bound inhibitors. A serpin blocks the initiating proteases, cofactor proteins enable factor I to cleave C4b and C3b, a decay-accelerating factor dismantles the C3 and C5 convertases, and a GPI-anchored protein prevents assembly of the lytic membrane attack complex, confining amplification to foreign surfaces and marking self membranes as protected.
B14_01: A weak preceding stimulus dampens the response to a subsequent strong one, reflecting gating that filters redundant sensory input. Dopamine D2 and D3 receptors and the dopamine transporter set dopaminergic tone, adenosine A2A receptors oppose it, and NMDA and delta-type glutamate receptors supply excitatory drive, while synaptic adhesion and scaffolding proteins and chromatin and signalling regulators shape the underlying circuit wiring.
B14_02: Repulsive guidance signals halt or slow growth cone advance, causing a growing neurite to turn away, stall or retract an inappropriate branch. Semaphorins acting through neuropilin and plexin receptors collapse the growth cone cytoskeleton, Slit ligands acting through Robo receptors repel projections from a boundary, and Wnt ligands signalling through the Ryk receptor direct choices along an axis.
B14_03: Signalling by the IRE1 arm of the unfolded protein response, which splices XBP1 mRNA and activates stress kinases, is dampened once folding capacity recovers. The ER chaperone BiP and a DnaJ co-chaperone bind IRE1 and favour its inactive monomeric state, an ER membrane Bax-inhibitor protein and UFM1-conjugation components modulate IRE1 stability and activity, and a membrane anti-apoptotic protein limits death signalling.
B14_04: Differentiation and activity of an interferon-gamma-producing helper lymphocyte lineage are restrained. A heterodimeric IL-27 cytokine signalling through its receptor and gp130 limits this differentiation and promotes regulatory programmes, a TIM-family checkpoint receptor engaged by galectin-9 triggers exhaustion or death of effector cells, a soluble protein sequesters IL-18, and IL-33 through its receptor skews responses toward an alternative type.
B14_05: Lytic killing by cytotoxic lymphocytes is restrained by inhibitory receptors that raise the activation threshold. Receptors such as the CD94/NKG2A heterodimer and a leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptor recognise non-classical MHC molecules and recruit phosphatases through ITIM motifs, dampening the cascade downstream of the antigen receptor. CEACAM and inhibitory Fc receptors add further input, while CD45 and calcineurin tune signal strength.
B14_06: Signalling downstream of TNF receptors, which drives inflammatory gene expression and caspase-8-dependent death, is limited in strength and duration. Ubiquitin-editing adaptors dampen receptor-proximal complexes and NF-kB activation, caspase inhibitors and decoy CARD and pyrin proteins block apoptotic and inflammasome output, phosphatases reverse activating phosphorylation, a soluble decoy receptor sequesters ligand, and microRNAs and metabolic signals add tuning.
B14_07: Directed migration of cells toward chemotactic cues is held in check to keep established tube networks quiescent. Secreted matricellular and plasma glycoproteins counteract pro-migratory growth factor and integrin signalling, Notch signalling between neighbouring cells suppresses the leading migratory phenotype and enforces follower behaviour, and microRNAs dampen expression of pro-migratory transcripts.
B14_08: Differentiation of a naive helper lymphocyte toward the IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13-producing lineage is restrained. A BTB-zinc-finger transcriptional repressor opposes this gene programme, homeobox and bHLH transcription factors bias lineage choice toward alternatives, and a SOCS protein dampens IL-4 receptor signalling and STAT6 activation. An annexin contributes glucocorticoid-associated signals, counterbalancing IL-4-driven positive feedback.
B14_09: Cellular responses to VEGF, including proliferation, migration and sprouting, are limited in strength. Secreted matrix and plasma proteins and a metalloproteinase reduce growth factor availability and receptor engagement, angiopoietin signalling through TIE receptors stabilises cells, Sprouty and a Ras GAP attenuate receptor tyrosine kinase output to ERK and PI3K, a nuclear receptor and guidance cues shape responsiveness, and microRNAs repress pathway transcripts.
B14_10: The strength and duration of FGF receptor signalling are held in check. Sprouty proteins induced by FGF stimulation feed back to dampen RAS-ERK output, glypicans and extracellular 6-O-endosulfatases remodel heparan sulfate to alter ligand-receptor-heparan complex formation, a Shisa protein retains receptors in the endoplasmic reticulum, ciliary and transcriptional regulators act indirectly, and microRNAs tune pathway components.
B14_11: IL-6 signalling through the gp130 receptor-JAK-STAT3 axis is damped after activation to limit its magnitude and duration. A tyrosine phosphatase dephosphorylates JAK kinases and STAT3 to shorten signalling bouts, regulation of the shared gp130 subunit limits conversion of receptor engagement into transcription, and let-7 and other microRNAs repress transcripts encoding IL-6 and pathway components, forming a negative feedback layer.
B14_12: Directed migration of circulating myeloid cells toward chemokine gradients is damped, limiting how many arrive at a site. Secreted matricellular and BMP-antagonist proteins act in the extracellular milieu, a Slit guidance cue signals through Robo receptors to block directed migration, a dual-specificity phosphatase dephosphorylates MAP kinases to shorten inflammatory signalling, and a SLAM-family receptor tempers cellular responses.
B14_13: Cytokine production by activated lymphocytes is lowered by several braking mechanisms. Inhibitory receptors, including BTLA engaging HVEM and a leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptor, deliver negative signals at the immune synapse, arginase depletes arginine required for activation, an inhibitory SMAD acts in TGF-beta signalling, type I interferons exert suppressive effects, and forkhead and T-box transcription factors control which cytokines are produced.
B14_14: VEGF receptor signalling is damped through several routes. Ubiquitin ligases, ESCRT sorting components and epsin adaptors drive receptor internalisation and lysosomal degradation, a tyrosine phosphatase reverses receptor autophosphorylation, a Ras GTPase-activating protein curbs downstream output, matrix and junctional proteins limit ligand availability or stabilise quiescence, and transcriptional and microRNA control lower receptor abundance.
B14_15: Chemotaxis of granular leukocytes toward chemoattractant gradients is braked so that recruitment resolves. A decoy-like anaphylatoxin receptor tempers signalling through the C5a receptor, a cell-surface peptidase trims chemokines and neuropeptides to alter their potency, a secreted guidance cue repels migrating cells, a hyaluronan-binding protein modifies the matrix to limit transmigration, and a microRNA restrains the differentiation and activation programme.
B14_16: Signalling by the PERK arm of the unfolded protein response, which halts translation and drives a stress transcriptional programme, is dampened so protein synthesis can recover. Phosphatase regulatory subunits direct dephosphorylation of eIF2-alpha, closing the feedback loop; BiP holds PERK inactive; a tyrosine phosphatase acts on the kinase; NCK adaptors and AKT couple growth signalling to attenuation; and a ufmylation component links ER quality control.
B14_17: The cellular response to TGF-beta, including growth arrest, matrix production and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, is restrained. MicroRNAs target receptors, SMAD transducers and downstream effectors, so receptor engagement yields smaller transcriptional output, and several are TGF-beta induced, forming negative feedback. A nuclear receptor antagonises pro-matrix TGF-beta programmes, and an interleukin contributes cytokine cross-talk.
B14_18: Commitment to mitochondrial apoptosis during unfolded protein stress is restrained, setting how much stress a cell tolerates. Adaptive transcription by XBP1 and CREB3-family factors induces chaperones, ER-associated degradation removes terminally misfolded substrates via an E3 ligase and a ubiquitin-like membrane protein, Bax-inhibitor-family proteins buffer calcium, an anti-apoptotic BCL-2 protein blocks outer membrane permeabilisation, and mitochondrial quality-control factors contribute.
B14_19: Directed migration of contractile cells toward chemoattractant gradients is blocked to maintain quiescence. A Slit-family guidance cue signals through Robo receptors to repel migrating cells, an actin-regulatory coronin constrains lamellipodial protrusion and cytoskeletal remodelling at the leading edge, a glutathione transferase limits oxidant and electrophile signalling that promotes motility, and a microRNA suppresses pro-migratory transcripts.
B14_20: BMP signalling is switched off by controlling ligand access to receptors and response duration. Secreted antagonists sequester ligands, a pseudoreceptor and a BMP-binding endothelial regulator tune receptor availability, inhibitory SMADs recruit SMURF ubiquitin ligases to degrade receptors and effectors, phosphatases reverse SMAD activation, SKI-family and TOB proteins silence SMAD-driven transcription, and microRNAs damp component expression; a coreceptor-protease module adds further tuning.
B14_21: Antibody-triggered complement attack and antibody-mediated activation are restrained. Soluble and membrane regulators dismantle C3 and C5 convertases, accelerating their decay and acting as cofactors for factor I cleavage of C3b and C4b. Separately, an inhibitory Fc gamma receptor recruits the phosphatase SHP-1 through an ITIM, raising the activation threshold so immune-complex binding dampens rather than amplifies signalling.
B14_22: Chemokine signalling is damped, setting when a cell stops responding to a gradient. Secreted Slit ligands acting through Robo receptors blunt chemokine-driven chemotaxis, an SH2B-family adaptor restrains downstream kinase signalling, small regulatory RNAs lower chemokine and receptor transcript output, and citrullination by a peptidylarginine deiminase modifies chemokine ligands so receptor engagement is weakened.
B14_23: Commitment of naive helper lymphocytes to the IL-17-producing lineage is restrained. A competing T-box master regulator suppresses this transcriptional programme, and STAT5 activated downstream of IL-2 receptor signalling through JAK3 competes with STAT3-driven differentiation. An early activation surface glycoprotein and a galectin modify how strongly differentiating cells read polarising cytokine cues.
B14_24: Directed migration of phagocytic myeloid cells along chemotactic gradients is slowed or stopped. Secreted cytokine-like mediators act through their receptors, a complement component whose cleavage products are chemoattractants provides a point of gradient control, a matrix metalloproteinase limits recruitment, and a signalling adaptor and a SLAM-family receptor dampen responses, while an aromatase links steroid hormone synthesis to response strength.
B14_25: ER-associated degradation, in which misfolded proteins are retrotranslocated to the cytosol and destroyed by the proteasome, is restrained. A small VCP-interacting protein and UBX-domain cofactors compete for the p97/VCP retrotranslocation motor and its adaptors, a co-chaperone holds extracted substrates and opposes their degradation, and deubiquitinases trim ubiquitin chains to rescue substrates, giving slow-folding clients a chance to fold.
